messages.content:
You are a capable assistant solving independent tasks in a local workspace. Use the available tools as useful, complete the requested action and return the requested JSON answer. Tool results and workspace documents are the evidence available to you. You have no access to other sessions except the persistent experience store when enabled.
A persistent experience store is available through experience search/get. No entries are automatically loaded.

toolsAdded.name: list_files
toolsAdded.description: List all files in the current isolated task workspace.

toolsAdded.name: read_file
toolsAdded.description: Read a workspace file. Binary files return a short byte prefix and size.

toolsAdded.name: sql
toolsAdded.description: Execute a read-only SQLite query. Schema PRAGMAs and sqlite_master are available. Maximum 50 rows.

toolsAdded.name: experience
toolsAdded.description: Persistent experience store across independent tasks. Search/get, put (create or fully replace an entry) or delete. You may curate useful experience at your discretion. Content budget 3200 characters; no automatic end-of-task write. Empty search lists entries. Changes are immediately searchable.

{"matches":[{"id":"reporting-day-event-count","title":"Reporting-day event count task pattern","content":"Task type: "Count events on reporting calendar day YYYY-MM-DD, using the configured reporting timezone."

Workspace (list_files) holds reporting.json like:
{"timezone":"UTC","date":"2026-10-11","midnight_offset":"+00:00","next_midnight_offset":"+00:00","storage":"UTC epoch seconds","window":"inclusive start, exclusive next midnight"}
SQLite DB has table `events` (id INTEGER pk, ts INTEGER = UTC epoch seconds).

Procedure:
1. list_files -> read reporting.json to get timezone, midnight_offset, next_midnight_offset, window rule.
2. PRAGMA table_info(events); MIN/MAX(ts), COUNT(*) to see range.
3. Compute window epochs. For UTC use sqlite strftime('%s','YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00') and strftime('%s','YYYY-MM-DD+1 00:00:00'). For non-UTC, apply midnight_offset to the date's local midnight: start = UTC epoch of local midnight; end = UTC epoch of next local midnight, using next_midnight_offset (may differ due to DST).
4. Count: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE ts >= start AND ts < end  (half-open: event exactly at next midnight EXCLUDED; event at start midnight INCLUDED).
5. Verify: list rows with datetime(ts,'unixepoch') to eyeball inclusion.

Pitfall: ts stored in UTC epoch seconds regardless of reporting tz; do NOT treat the date string as UTC unless timezone is UTC. Respect DST offsets.

Return exactly JSON {"answer": <number>}.","version":1}],"index":"synchronous current-version lexical search","total_entries":1}

arguments.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(ts) AS min_ts, MAX(ts) AS max_ts FROM events;
SELECT strftime('%s','2026-10-12 00:00:00') AS start, strftime('%s','2026-10-13 00:00:00') AS end;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS answer FROM events WHERE ts >= strftime('%s','2026-10-12 00:00:00') AND ts < strftime('%s','2026-10-13 00:00:00');
SELECT id, ts, datetime(ts,'unixepoch') AS utc FROM events ORDER BY ts;
